technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the increment as a Java-based Mule extension using the existing Mule domain, application deployment, DeploymentService, connector, and MuleEvent APIs rather than modifying Mule runtime internals.
Represent domain lifecycle operations as deploy, undeploy, and redeploy services, with redeploy applying the updated domain configuration to all applications associated with the domain.
Implement application property overrides as deployment-time values with precedence over packaged application properties, while preserving the packaged defaults.
Use an XML schema for the AMQP transport configuration so that IDE validation and autocomplete are available.
Use a reusable global AMQP configuration containing shared connection and transport attributes; flow-level endpoints reference this configuration.
Use a standard AMQP client library and a connection/channel abstraction managed by the Mule connector lifecycle.
Implement continuous consumption as an inbound message source that listens to a queue, converts each message into a MuleEvent, and dispatches it to a configured flow.
Implement instant consumption as a request operation that can be invoked at an arbitrary point in a flow and returns the consumed message as a MuleEvent or operation result.
Use explicit acknowledgement and error-handling behavior, with acknowledgement occurring only after successful message processing unless configured otherwise.
Provide a base project skeleton with stable placeholders for endpoints, connectors, transactions, configuration, lifecycle management, tests, and documentation.
Use automated unit tests, broker-backed integration tests, deployment lifecycle tests, and schema validation tests as the primary verification strategy.
assumptions: The existing Mule source tree, build system, extension APIs, domain APIs, and DeploymentService are available and buildable.
The target Mule runtime and API version are known to the development team and do not require compatibility across multiple major Mule versions.
Domain deployment, application deployment, undeployment, and application update primitives already exist and only need to be composed or extended for the requested behavior.
A compatible AMQP broker, such as RabbitMQ, is available for integration testing.

AMQP requirements are limited to queue consumption and the configuration needed by those consumption modes; publishing, exchanges, routing administration, clustering, and advanced broker management are out of scope.
Security support is limited to the existing Mule or AMQP client mechanisms for credentials, TLS, and connection settings; no new enterprise security subsystem is required.
The specification and schema are delivered as repository documentation and versioned artifacts; formal external product-owner or community review time is not included.
The developer is responsible for implementation, tests, documentation, build updates, and local integration verification, but not production rollout or operational support.
The estimates represent productive work effort in workdays and exclude elapsed waiting time for reviews, external dependencies, or environment provisioning.

activities.activity_description: Analyze U1-U8, map each requirement to Mule APIs and extension components, define lifecycle behavior, property precedence, AMQP consumption semantics, error handling, acknowledgement rules, and interfaces for the implementation.

Create or update the project structure, build configuration, module layout, package conventions, configuration placeholders, endpoint and connector abstractions, transaction placeholders, lifecycle interfaces, and initial test layout required by U5.

Define the XML schema and associated metadata for global AMQP configuration, connection attributes, queue endpoints, continuous consumers, instant-consumption operations, message options, and validation constraints required by U4.

Implement the single-point AMQP transport configuration, including connection parameters, credentials references, host and port settings, virtual host, TLS-related options supported by the existing platform, and reuse by flow-level endpoints as required by U6.

Implement AMQP client integration, connector lifecycle management, connection and channel creation, resource cleanup, message conversion, configuration validation, and common exception handling used by both consumption modes.

Implement the inbound AMQP listener that continuously consumes queue messages, creates MuleEvents, dispatches them to a flow, applies acknowledgement and error behavior, and supports start, stop, and reconnect lifecycle operations for U7.

Implement a flow operation that consumes an AMQP message on demand at any point in a flow, applies timeout and empty-queue behavior, converts the result into the expected Mule representation, and releases or reuses broker resources for U8.

Implement domain deploy, undeploy, and redeploy orchestration through the Mule API, including association of applications with domains, undeploying dependent applications, updating all applications during redeploy, lifecycle ordering, and failure reporting for U1.

Extend or integrate DeploymentService usage to deploy a new application with deployment-time property overrides, define override precedence and validation, propagate values to the application configuration, and report deployment errors for U2.

Write and organize the reviewed functional and technical specifications, document configuration examples, deployment behavior, AMQP usage, supported placeholders, and contribution guidance so product owners and community members can review and provide feedback for U3.

Implement tests for schema validation, configuration reuse, connection lifecycle, message conversion, acknowledgement and error paths, continuous and instant consumption, domain lifecycle operations, application property overrides, and broker-backed integration scenarios.

Update build and packaging metadata, include schema and documentation artifacts, configure automated test execution, verify dependency and license integration, and validate installation and execution in a representative Mule runtime.

Run end-to-end scenarios covering domain and application deployment together with AMQP flows, diagnose and fix integration defects, perform code cleanup and API consistency checks, and finalize the increment for delivery.
